description.value: The study investigated neural correlates of impaired cognitive control during a Stroop task in individuals with methamphetamine dependence compared with healthy controls, and examined relationships between brain activation, task performance, drug-use characteristics, and impulsivity.

design.value: A cross-sectional between-group fMRI study using a manual, two-condition Stroop task. The fMRI analysis used an ANCOVA with group as a between-subjects factor, task condition as a within-subjects factor, and age as a covariate; behavioral data were analyzed using a two-way ANOVA and Mann–Whitney U tests, and exploratory Spearman correlations were performed.

description.value: A German version of the impulsive behavior scale exploring four dimensions of impulsivity: lack of premeditation, urgency, sensation seeking, and lack of perseverance.
The criteria for methamphetamine dependence and psychiatric disorders were established using the M.I.N.I. interview by trained study personnel.

description.value: A manual Stroop test with congruent and incongruent conditions requiring participants to indicate the color of presented stimuli by pressing one of two buttons.

clinical_characteristics.value: MA abusers reported MA consumption for approximately 15.3 years (SD = 6.1) on average; the mean age of beginning first MA consumption was 17.8 years (SD = 4.0), and methamphetamine abstinence at measurement averaged 8.3 ± 6.4 days.

education_summary.value: The MA group had a median of nine years schooling.

description.value: Healthy subjects without substance abuse or dependence, other psychiatric disorders, or neurological disorders.

exclusion_criteria.value: criteria for substance abuse or dependence or other psychiatric disorders according to DSM-IV criteria

education_summary.value: Control subjects had a median of 12 years schooling.

task_name.value: manual version of the Stroop test

task_description.value: The task consisted of two conditions: a congruent (CC) and an incongruent condition (IC). In the CC, 18 color words were presented in the color denoted by the corresponding word; in the IC, 18 color words were displayed in one of three colors that were not denoted by the word. Participants indicated the color as fast as possible by pressing one of two buttons.

presentation_software.value: Presentation software (Neurobehavioral Systems Inc., Albany, California)

instructions.value: All subjects were instructed to indicate as fast as possible the type of color by pressing one of two buttons.

stimuli.value: 18 congruent and 18 incongruent color-word stimuli, with two possible answers presented in the lower visual field.

modality.value: resting-state fMRI and Stroop task fMRI

instrument.value: MAGNETOM PRISMA FIT, Siemens Healthineers, Erlangen, Germany, equipped with a 64-element head matrix coil

description.value: A series of 220 whole-brain volume sets was acquired in one session. T2*-weighted images were obtained using a multiband multislice GE-EPI sequence with 104 contiguous transverse slices covering the entire brain and including the lower brainstem.

instrument.value: MAGNETOM PRISMA FIT, Siemens Healthineers, Erlangen, Germany

description.value: High-resolution anatomical T1-weighted volume scans were obtained in sagittal orientation.

Functional images were slice-time corrected, corrected for head motion, co-registered to the T1 reference using boundary-based registration, normalized to MNI space using nonlinear registration, and spatially smoothed with a 6 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: The functional images were slice-time corrected using 3dTshift from AFNI.
Structural T1 image was adjusted for intensity non-uniformity and the non-brain tissue was removed.
The functional images were co-registered to the T1 reference using bbregister (FreeSurfer), which implements boundary-based registration.
T1 images were normalized to the MNI space by applying nonlinear registration using ANTs.
The derived transformation parameters were used to normalize the functional images.
Spatially smoothed with the Gaussian kernel of 6 mm FWHM using mcflirt.
The first four images were discarded.

model_settings.value: The data were high-pass filtered with a cutoff period of 128 s, corrected for serial correlations choosing AR(1), and analyzed voxel-wise to calculate statistical parametric maps of t statistics for condition specific effects.

Between-subjects factor group (MA vs HC), within-subjects factor task (CC vs. IC), and age as a covariate. Whole-brain group comparisons were thresholded at voxel-level p < 0.001 uncorrected with a minimum cluster size of k ≥ 16; clusters were also assessed with FWE correction for multiple comparisons at p < 0.05.
One between-subjects factor group (MA vs. HC) and one within-subjects factor condition (CC vs. IC) for reaction time.

Correlations used Stroop accuracy and mean parameter estimates from significant clusters in the left DLPFC, anterior midcingulate cortex, and V1/V2; parameter estimates were also correlated with duration of drug consumption, age of starting crystal meth consumption, and UPPS total score.
